reason: The cited evidence shows Mo improves passivation (E1, E3) and that refined/amorphous structures can form protective oxide layers with good tribocorrosion resistance (E2), but none of the passages demonstrate that nanocrystalline refinement itself promotes passive film formation, that boron doping refines grains or aids passivation, or that a passive film simultaneously reduces wear and corrosion synergistically. The key mechanistic premises are largely unsupported by the specific evidence provided.
premises: Nanocrystalline grain refinement promotes formation of a uniform, adherent passive oxide film
Mo addition stabilizes the passive film and improves passivation/corrosion resistance
Boron doping induces beneficial precipitates that support grain refinement
The passive oxide film acts as a dual barrier reducing both corrosive ion transport and mechanical wear
Combined wear-corrosion degradation is less than the sum of individual effects due to film synergy
